name: Aguascalientes
summary_text: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score. The dossier's only Aguascalientes-specific findings are resident-facing: Human Rights Watch (March 2025) lists it among states that have not reformed their legislation at all to create a legal gender recognition procedure, and it has no enacted state-level non-discrimination protection on sexual orientation or gender identity (a February 2025 initiative was still only an initiative). No region-specific incident, enforcement or ordinance evidence was found.

sources.title: Trans Rights in Mexico: Progress and Challenges | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (HRW blocked the fetch); the underlying Human Rights Watch news feature (31 March 2025) surveys progress and challenges for trans rights in Mexico, including the state-by-state patchwork of legal gender recognition that the country dossier uses to identify the few states that have reformed.

sources.title: “I Just Want to Contribute to Society”: The Need for Legal Gender Recognition in Tabasco, Mexico | HRW
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (HRW report PDF not cached); the underlying Human Rights Watch report (March 2024) documents the human-rights cost of the absence of legal gender recognition in Tabasco - the dossier's reference case for how non-reforming states, Aguascalientes among them, leave trans people without any lawful marker procedure.

sources.title: Transfemicide becomes a crime in a ‘watershed’ moment for Mexico City | Transgender | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: Guardian global-development report (24 July 2024) on Mexico City making transfemicide a criminal offence - the country dossier uses this reform benchmark to contrast the capital and pioneer states with the non-reforming majority, which includes Aguascalientes.
